name: ws-6ee05547-blind29-ots
instr:
# gobwas/ws — a WebSocket toolkit misbehaving from handshake to compression, without a test suite

This is a toolkit for speaking a packet-oriented protocol over a long-lived socket, both as the side that opens a connection and as the side that accepts one. The repository has received 29 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about the protocol changed and nothing about the calling programs changed, yet traffic that used to cross a connection now goes wrong at nearly every stage.

Taking data off a connection is where it shows first. Asking the incremental consumer for the next packet on a perfectly ordinary stream is refused as though the packet's type byte were one of the values the protocol keeps in reserve, and this happens for plain text packets, for continuations of them and for pings alike, so no payload is obtained at all. Putting a size limit in place and feeding an over-long packet produces that same blanket refusal instead of the too-large complaint it should give.

Once packets can be obtained again, a message that arrives in several parts still fails in several further, distinct places. Consuming the body of a multi-part message stops with an error at the first part boundary rather than continuing into the following part, and a stream that stops in the middle of a payload signals something other than the truncated-input error. Independently of that, the step that advances to the following part consults the hook meant for in-between packets exactly when no such hook
